title: Eleven Days and One Decision
subtitle: 挫折振作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 挫折振作（做人与做事·挫折与失败）
meta: 主题语境：挫折振作（做人与做事·挫折与失败）　|　核心词汇：crisis　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crisis 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 my father ① faced a crisis that had been building for eleven months, and he said the facing was the whole of the deciding. The ② crisis, meaning the turning point and not the trouble, lasted eleven days and stayed that sharp; crisis, he said, is the only thing in a year that is judged by how soon it is met.

Every ③ crisis in that business had the same hour of the night, and the ④ crisis at the end, meaning the one he kept from the bank and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever spoke of twice. Crisis, my mother said, is nine parts hour and one part somebody willing to meet it; my father said the meeting is the part that fills eleven days.

My grandmother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the crisis was the whole of the illness, meaning the turning and not the trouble. The ⑥ crisis, meaning the turning and not any of that, is the only thing in an illness that everybody watches for and nobody names; crisis, she said, is either something you face or the only word that means both a turning point and a turning. He said the turning is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ crisis had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the hour. The ⑧ crisis of the whole thing, my father wrote in January, was one decision and thirty years of meeting; crisis, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to meet it. She said the meeting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ crisis I remember is the one at the end, which passed in 1976 and is still described as the sharpest in the county. A ⑩ crisis, my mother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being met; every crisis, she said, is a turning that has agreed to look like a turning point. She said the turning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 危机；危急关头
B. n. 危机（指那个转折点本身，与那些麻烦相对）
C. 固定搭配：face a crisis 面对危机
D. n. 危机（指那门生意里每一次）
E. n. 危机（指末尾那一次）
F. n. 转折点；危象（医学上指病情的转机时刻）
G. n. 危机（指报告里提到的那一次）
H. n. 紧要关头；决定性时刻（抽象总称）

items.q: faced a crisis that had been building for eleven months
The crisis, meaning the turning point and not the trouble
the crisis was the whole of the illness
the crisis had become a line in a report
The crisis of the whole thing
A crisis, my mother said in 1978

answers.why: face a crisis 意为“面对危机”，1962 年父亲面对一场已经酝酿了十一个月的危机。
crisis 意为“危机”，指那个转折点本身而不是那些麻烦，它持续了十一天。
crisis 指那门生意里每一次危机，每一次都发生在夜里同样的时辰。
crisis 指末尾那一次（他对银行隐瞒的那一次），是唯一有人提起过两次的。
crisis 意为“转折点、危象”（医学用语），祖母说转机就是那场病的全部，指的是病情的转折时刻而不是那些麻烦。
crisis 为医学用法，指病情的转折时刻而不是那些麻烦，是病中人人都在等、却无人说破的东西。
crisis 意为“危机”，指报告里提到的那一次，到 1970 年这次危机成了报告里的一行。
crisis 意为“紧要关头、决定性时刻”，父亲一月写道，整件事的紧要关头是一个决定三十年的直面。
crisis 意为“危机、危急关头”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1976 年过去，至今仍被说成全县最尖锐的。
crisis 为抽象总称，母亲说一场危机是唯一会因为被直面而变好的东西。
